An exponential growth model can be written in the form $M(w) = a(1 + r)^{w}$, where $M(w)$ is the value after $w$ time periods, $a$ is the initial value, and $r$ is the growth rate expressed as a decimal. It's given that the initial value of the coin was $$585$, so $a = 585$. It's also given that the value increases by $3\%$ each year, so $r = 0.03$. Substituting these values into the exponential growth model yields $M(w) = 585(1 + 0.03)^{w}$, which is equivalent to $M(w) = 585(1.03)^{w}$.
